newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee council sees need to up gov't sales.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee council sees need to up gov't sales.

text.p: Members of Brazil's new coffee council have reached a consensus that sales from government stocks of up to 300,000 60-kg bags a month are necessary until the end of the June, an exporter official said.
Currently monthly sales are limited to 200,000 bags.

Members discussed the issue at an informal session yesterday in Brasilia ahead of the first official meeting of the Conselho Deliberativo da Politica do Cafe (CDPC) to be held on February 24 in Vitoria, Espirito Santo state.

"We evaluated the situation and reached the consensus that sales of stocks of up to 300,000 bags a month were necessary until June," said Oswaldo Aranha, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Federation.

Aranha said it was not certain however a definite decision to raise the ceiling of the monthly auctions would be taken at next week's council session as government officials needed to assess how best to hold the sales.
Members of the council will hold a further informal session on the morning of February 24 ahead of the official council meeting to be held at 1430 local/1730 GMT, he said.

Apart from ensuring the flow of coffee to the domestic and internal markets, the council is also expected to discuss producer debts which yesterday a government official estimated totalled around 700 million reais with Banco do Brasil.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
